## Rules that apply to every prompt

# Project: 26.humza.website (birthday quiz)

## Stack

- npm workspaces + Turborepo (npm only, never pnpm/yarn)
- apps/web: React 19 + Vite. Routes: /play (phones), /screen (projector), /host (control panel)
- apps/worker: Hono on Cloudflare Workers + one Durable Object class `Room` (WebSocket Hibernation API, SQLite storage, alarms)
- packages/shared: Zod schemas, pure game logic (reducer, scoring, awards, time sync, rate limiter, troll rules)
- packages/emails: React Email templates, sent via Resend
- Post-game persistence: Neon Postgres + Drizzle, RLS enabled on every table
- Photos: Cloudflare R2
- Tests: Vitest (unit + component via Testing Library + jsdom), @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (DO/Worker), Playwright (e2e), Node bot harness (load)

## Architecture rules

- The server is authoritative. Clients send intents and render state. They never compute scores, timers or phase changes.
- All game logic is a pure reducer in packages/shared: `reduce(state, event, now) -> { state, effects }`. The DO is a thin shell that feeds events in and executes effects (broadcast, set alarm, persist). This is what makes everything unit-testable.
- Time is always injected (`now: number`), never `Date.now()` inside logic.
- Browser APIs (wakeLock, vibrate, getUserMedia, Audio) are wrapped in small adapters so tests can mock them.

## Testing rules (non-negotiable)

- Every feature has at least one test file, named in the phase prompt. Write the tests first or alongside the code, never after "it works".
- Never skip, `.only`, or delete a failing test to get green. Fix the code or ask.
- Pure logic → plain Vitest. DO behaviour → vitest-pool-workers. UI → Testing Library. Cross-device flows → Playwright.
- A phase is done only when `npm run test:unit` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Scripts

- Naming: `<domain>:<action>` (e.g. `test:unit`, `questions:check`, `email:preview`, `dev:jump`)

- This is a separate birthday project. Never change LifeSmart, use its production resources or copy its pupil-specific rules into this project.
- The plan's agreed decisions take precedence over its suggested defaults. Later explicit user decisions take precedence over both. Record material implementation choices.
- Baseer presents and Humza controls. Guests play individually. No pods, guest accounts, CMS, compulsory scoring floor or automatic score multipliers.
- Keep questions in versioned server-side TypeScript. Public question data is a deliberate projection that excludes correct answers, scoring secrets and future reveals.
- One Worker serves the application and API; one SQLite-backed Durable Object owns each room. Neon and email stay outside the live guest-action path. Image/audio processing also stays outside it.
- Persist accepted actions before success acknowledgements. Make retries idempotent. Memory is a cache. Use one durable scheduler to own all room alarms.
- Identity uses random game-scoped credentials. Device information is separately associated context, never an identity fingerprint or authority for scoring.
- Use React, TypeScript, Vite, Hono, Cloudflare Workers/Durable Objects/R2, Neon, Better Auth and Resend as specified in the plan. Use a small shared validation package and consistent styling primitives. Verify current official documentation when implementing version-sensitive APIs; pin compatible dependencies and retain the lockfile.
- Use domain folders, British English, accessible controls and clear phone states. Include reduced-motion support and optional audio. Keep secrets and personal diagnostics off the projector.
- Do not open, quote, or commit secret files such as `.env`, `.dev.vars`, private keys, or credential files. Example templates may be read.
- Work in the existing implementation. Do not create competing state stores, socket clients, auth factories, schedulers, schemas or score engines for each new feature.
- Keep production paths real. Deterministic local fakes are allowed only behind explicit test/development adapters; they must not silently succeed in deployed environments.
- Implement, run relevant checks, fix failures and update documentation. Do not rewrite unrelated work or weaken checks to obtain a pass.
- No deployments, paid resource creation or changes to unrelated remote resources are implied by Prompts 01-18. Missing external credentials should not prevent completing locally testable work; report precisely what remains unverified.
- Agent instructions are edited in `.agents`. Run `npm run agents:sync` afterwards. Do not hand-edit the generated copies.
- At the end of every stage update `docs/build-progress.md`: status, files/interfaces added, decisions/defaults, commands and results, manual verification, unresolved issues and the exact next stage. Never label an unrun check as passed.
- Final response for each stage: what now works, how to run/try it, what was verified and any concrete remaining limitation. Do not automatically begin the next prompt.

# Admin coverage

Every feature ships with its admin view in the same change. A feature is not done until the host can **see** it, **manage** it and **rehearse** it from `/admin`, without asking guests to help.

## The registry is the source of truth

`apps/web/src/admin/features.ts` lists every feature (`adminFeatures`). The sidebar, the page titles and the room overview cards are built from it. Each entry has:

- `id`, `label`, `scope` (`global` under `/admin`, `room` under `/admin/rooms/:gameId`) and `path`.
- `summary`: what the page shows, in one sentence.
- `rehearsal`: what the host can try with no guests (a preview, sample, demo or dry run). Be concrete. "None" is not acceptable. If something truly needs live guests, say how to do it with a second browser tab.
- `owns`: the top-level source folders the feature lives in (`apps/api/src/<domain>`, `apps/web/src/<domain>`). Each folder belongs to exactly one feature.
- `status` (room features): a short live line for the overview card, read from the host snapshot.

Shared plumbing that is not a feature goes in `adminExempt` with a reason. Do not exempt something to avoid building its view.

`apps/web/src/admin/features.test.ts` enforces this. It fails when a source folder has no owner, a folder is owned twice, an owned folder no longer exists, a feature has no summary or rehearsal, or an `/admin` route and a registry entry do not match. Never weaken the test to get a pass; add the view.

## What a feature's admin view must have

1. **See.** The current state, live from the host snapshot (`useAdminRoom`) for room features, or from a validated section read (`readSection`) for global ones. Show counts, who did what and when, and anything waiting on the host. Include history, not just what is happening now.
2. **Manage.** Every host action for the feature, as a host command (`execute(...)` → `/api/rooms/play` → `readHostDetails` → `applyHostAction`). Commands are receipted, validated again inside the room, and roll back on error. Give each one a notice in `command-notices.ts` and a `CommandScope` for its feedback.
3. **Rehearse.** A way to try it without guests: render the real phone and stage component with sample data (frame previews, troll previews, question rehearsal), or a demo or dry-run command. Use real components, never a mock-up that can drift.
4. **Safe defaults.** Anything that reaches the projector or guests can be switched off or undone from the page.

## Server side

- Host-only data goes in the snapshot only for `audience === "control"`, as an optional field on `lobbySnapshotSchema` with exact Zod limits. Never send it to the stage or guests.
- Add host actions to the `commands` list in `routes.ts`, to `readHostDetails` (validate every field), to `PartyRoom.hostAction` and to `applyHostAction`. Validate again in the domain function; the room does not trust its caller.

## Tests for each feature's admin view

- A room spec for each host command: success, refusal and replay.
- A component test for the admin page using `controls.test-support.tsx` (`setupControls`, `mountControls`): each control sends the right command.
- A snapshot test proving host-only fields are absent for stage and guest audiences.

## Checklist for a new feature

1. Build the feature.
2. Add or extend its entry in `adminFeatures`, with `owns` covering its folders.
3. Add the route in `apps/web/src/routes.tsx`, and the path to `admin-return.ts`.
4. Build the see, manage and rehearse view.
5. Add the tests above, and run `features.test.ts`.
6. Update `docs/data-inventory.md` if it stores anything new, and `docs/build-progress.md`.

## Scoped rules

### Server-side question packs

Applies to `apps/api/src/questions/**/*.ts`.

# Questions

- Keep the party script in versioned TypeScript in this folder. There is no CMS and no client-side question pack.
- Public snapshots exclude correct answers, scoring secrets, and future reveals.
- Do not copy answer keys or truth nicknames into `apps/web`.
- The pack a room plays is the one named by its stored version. The illustrative demo stays `demo-2026-09-22` until a birthday version is explicitly released.
- New party questions are files in `apps/api/src/questions/packs/birthday/`, registered on the catalogue and left out of the running order while they are drafts. Do not invent party questions, and do not edit the demo pack to hold them.

### Question authoring workflow

Applies to `apps/api/src/questions/**/*.ts` and `docs/question-authoring.md`.

# Question authoring

Read `docs/question-authoring.md` before adding or editing a question. Party questions are TypeScript files, not a CMS.

Recognise:

- "Next question idea: …"
- "Add a question where …"
- "Make this question ready."
- "Move this question before …"
- "Change the answer/options for …"
- "Now customise the design of this question."

For a new idea:

1. Read the birthday manifest, `authoring.ts`, `defaults.ts`, and any related question.
2. Choose an existing mechanic when it fits: choice (with a correct, poll, or threshold outcome), typed, wordle, slider, rank, vote, guess, duel, or finale.
3. Create `apps/api/src/questions/packs/birthday/<id>.ts` with the matching helper. The id and filename are a stable slug, with no running-order number.
4. Apply defaults from `defaults.ts` for ordinary settings the user did not specify.
5. Keep the user's wording. Record a material assumption in the question file only when it changes the mechanic.
6. Record a missing answer or asset with `{ missing: { code, name, detail } }` or a required media ref that has no `asset`. Do not invent the fact, the person, or the file.
7. Import the question in `packs/birthday/manifest.ts` `catalogue`. Do not add a draft to `order`. Do not change `startDemo`, the demo pack, a room, or a deployment.
8. Run `npm run content:check`.
9. Report the id, mechanic, draft or ready status, and anything still missing.

Wordle uses `wordleQuestion` with a supplied five-letter uppercase target. The default is six guesses, two minutes and 100 points for a solve. Keep the target and dictionary server-side; never substitute ordinary typed matching. Use the real authenticated phone rehearsal to check feedback.

Ask a short question only when the ambiguity changes the meaning or the mechanic. Otherwise save a draft.

If the interaction is not one of these mechanics, explain the gap and still save a draft. Do not force the wrong mechanic or rewrite scoring.

A later edit finds the existing file by id. Reordering changes `order` in the manifest only. "Make this question ready" fills real supplied facts and, once it validates, still does not enter `order` unless the user asked to include it.

"Now customise the design of this question" keeps the same id and mechanic. Add the slug to `customPresentationIds` in `packages/shared`, set `presentation` on the question, write the design in `apps/web/src/play/designs/<slug>.tsx` with the shared kit, and register it in `designs/registry.ts`. Follow the full-screen question experience rule. Check the actual question in Admin → Question packs → Phone preview, plus `/design` for stand-in reveal states in development. Do not put the answer key in the client.

Do not edit a released pack's question files in place. A content change needs a new version id. Rooms keep the version they stored.

# Worker and room

- One Worker serves the application and API. One SQLite-backed Durable Object owns each room. One durable scheduler owns all room alarms.
- Persist an accepted action before its success acknowledgement. Retries use the same idempotency key.
- Neon, email, and image or audio processing stay outside the live guest-action path.

# Web app

- Follow the design and motion rules. Open the live library docs listed there before copying a component; ease every visible change.

### Full-screen party questions, clear phone actions and presentation flow

Applies to `apps/web/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/**/*.css` and `apps/api/src/questions/**/*.ts` and `docs/question-authoring.md`.

# Question experience

- This is a hosted Kahoot/Jackbox-style party game: Baseer presents, Humza advances the show, guests act on their phones. Design each round as a short presentation with get-ready, answer, sending, locked-in, reveal and score beats. The server owns when each beat occurs.
- Phone questions occupy the usable screen, with one unmistakable instruction, the question and generous answer controls. Keep the primary send action in the existing phone dock. Use the shared `QuestionExperience` frame and real `GuestPlay` renderer; bespoke designs keep their own identity inside that frame.
- Make the next action explicit: “Pick one, then send”, “Slide to your estimate”, or “Locked in — watch the stage”. Clearly distinguish selected, sending and server-accepted answers. Do not label an optimistic selection accepted in a live game.
- Use deliberate space and large type. Ordinary two-to-six-option questions should fit a phone screen; long ballots, long wording, keyboard entry and enlarged text may scroll vertically. Never clip an answer or shrink essential text just to fit. Check 320, 390 and 430px widths, a short landscape viewport, safe areas and zoom.
- Keep photo, sound, recovery and troll-selection tools secondary. Incoming troll notices and escape controls remain visible. Do not make these tools compete with the question or send button.
- Each question can have its own composition, motif and interaction treatment. Do not force every design into the same card grid. Reuse shared controls, theme variables, presentation registry and mechanics; never fork the socket, score engine or scheduler for a visual.
- Animate every meaningful change: question/phase entry, option selection, input feedback, submission, waiting, reveal, score and list/layout changes. Use Motion and the existing motion kit with eased timing, springs and short staggered entrances. Keep options stable and usable while the clock runs; decorative animation must not delay an action, cover text or leave an outgoing phase interactive.
- Respect reduced motion with short opacity/colour fades, no loops, parallax or travel. Never gate meaning on animation, sound or colour alone. Keep audio optional and stage wording readable across a room.
- Admin Question packs and individual question pages must offer a phone rehearsal using the actual guest renderer and server-projected public question fields. A rehearsal is isolated: no live room, socket, score, persistence or fabricated answer key. Label stand-in players, incomplete drafts and unsupported mechanics. Do not invent slider bounds or pretend a placeholder is the finished mechanic.
- When customising a question, verify its get-ready, answering, selected, pending, accepted, paused and reveal states in the admin preview/design bench and meaningful tests. Keep answer keys, notes and future reveals out of preview payloads. Add private admin details only to their existing authenticated inspection route.

# Design and motion

Maximise the libraries below. Reach for their current components, primitives, and effects first. Install and pin a missing package when a screen needs it. Do not invent a parallel primitive kit or one-off visual language beside `apps/web/src/ui`.

Before using or copying anything, open the live site (and the specific component or API page). Do not reconstruct APIs, class names, or install commands from memory. If the page and training data disagree, the page wins.

Compose those libraries into the existing surfaces (phone, stage, host, admin, results). Do not copy LifeSmart branding. Keep British English, large tappable phone controls, and stage type readable from across a room.

Screen colours come from `apps/web/src/theme/themes.ts`. A theme also has a skin, so the chrome fits the idea. Follow the theme rule when adding or changing one. Category and brand icons come from the packs listed in that rule: Lucide, Simple Icons, Game Icons, and Material Design Icons, rendered with `@iconify/react/dist/offline`.

## Fluid motion

Every visible change is eased. Nothing snaps: hover, press, focus, disabled, open/close, mount/unmount, list insert/remove/reorder, page or phase change, loading, success, and error. Subtle motion is required; instant `display`, un-eased colour cuts, and zero-duration transitions are not.

Use Motion springs or shared duration/easing tokens. Prefer enter/exit and layout animation over CSS that only styles the resting state. Decorative loops belong on the stage or idle screens, not on controls a guest must hit quickly.

```tsx
// ❌ BAD — appears and vanishes instantly
{
  open ? <Panel /> : null;
}

// ✅ GOOD — eased presence, still uses the shared panel
<AnimatePresence>
  {open ? (
    <motion.div
      initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 8 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
      exit={{ opacity: 0, y: 8 }}
    >
      <Panel />
    </motion.div>
  ) : null}
</AnimatePresence>;
```

## Reduced motion and stage safety

Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`. Turn off loops, parallax, blur storms, and layout thrash. Keep a short opacity or colour fade for state changes so the UI still does not pop. Motion must never hide a question, option, score, or answer on the projector, and must never put secrets or personal diagnostics on stage.

### Party themes are a palette plus a skin that fits the idea

Applies to `apps/web/src/theme/**/*.ts` and `apps/web/src/theme/**/*.tsx` and `apps/web/src/theme/**/*.css`.

# Themes

A theme is not a colour swap. It is a palette plus a skin that makes the shared chrome feel like the idea. Phones and the projector choose a theme separately. The choice is not pushed by the room.

Recognise:

- "Add a theme …"
- "New palette for …"
- "Make a theme where …"

Read these before editing:

- `apps/web/src/theme/themes.ts` for colours, roles, categories, and `DEFAULT_THEME_ID`
- `apps/web/src/theme/skins.ts` for families
- `apps/web/src/theme/theme-skin.css` for grounds and corner tokens
- `apps/web/src/theme/wordmark.tsx` for marks
- `apps/web/src/theme/install.ts` for how `data-theme` and `data-skin` are applied

## Palette

Add the palette in `themes.ts`. That file is the only place colour values are written.

- The id is lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens. The object key matches the id. The display name may keep punctuation.
- Fill every palette role: background, foreground, muted, accent, accentForeground, highlight, highlightForeground, surface, surfaceForeground, line, mark, markQuiet.
- Set `colorScheme` from the ground. Use `light` when the ground is cream, paper, white, or yellow. Otherwise use `dark`.
- Accent and highlight are both text on the page background and fills for buttons. Both pairs need contrast, and so do their foreground colours on those fills. `mark` on `markQuiet` stays strong enough for a join code.
- List the theme in exactly one `themeCategories` group. A missing or repeated id fails the typecheck.
- Leave `DEFAULT_THEME_ID` as `26-basic` unless the user asks to change the party default.
- Do not recolour `apps/web/public/favicon.svg`. It stays the 26 basic mark.

## Skin

`26-basic` is the only plain theme. Every other theme has an entry in `skins.ts`. The map is every theme id except `26-basic`, so a new theme that only has colours fails typecheck.

Choose the skin for the idea, not for whichever family was used last.

1. Join an existing family when that ground, shape, mark, and finish already say the idea. School lines, a nightclub stripe, a terminal grid, a floodlight, and a foil edge are families. Reuse them.
2. Add a ground, shape, or mark only when no family fits. Put the ground in `theme-skin.css`, built from the theme's own variables (`--background`, `--surface`, `--accent`, `--highlight`, `--line`). Take the mark from the icon packs below. Draw a new stroke in `wordmark.tsx` only when none of those packs has a fitting icon.
3. Do not leave the new theme on the plain chrome.

The skin changes the shared frame only:

- **Ground.** A fixed layer behind the page. It never sits on a question, option, score, or answer.
- **Shape.** `--radius-control` and `--radius-panel` on the shared controls.
- **Mark.** The navbar 26, shown from `data-mark`.
- **Finish.** How solid the frame is: `solid`, `glass`, `cartoon`, `realistic`, `minimal`, or `extravagant`. Pick the one that fits the idea. `26 basic` stays `solid`. Glass keeps a readable plate over the ground, and reduced motion turns its blur off. Cartoon is a thick outline and a hard shadow, with no bounce. Realistic is depth only. A finish never outlines the heading, never covers an option, and never loops.
- **Motif.** An optional static icon on the ground: `none`, `crest`, `scatter`, or `bleed`. Use `none` when the ground pattern is already the picture, including `26 basic`. Company marks come from Simple Icons. Other motifs come from Lucide. The icon stays behind the question.

Question flow, scoring, and copy stay put. Do not add a looping animation on a control or a question. Reduced motion already removes the corner transition.

## Deep layer

A skin family also has a deep layer in `apps/web/src/theme/deep-skins.ts`, drawn by `theme-deep.css`. It goes beyond the surface, so two themes in different families feel like different products, not recolours. Every family except 26 basic's `plain` needs an entry; `deep-skins.test.ts` fails otherwise.

- **Type.** `grotesk`, `serif`, `mono`, `condensed`, `rounded`, `slab` or `italic`: sets `--font-display` and `--font-sans` and the heading case. Use system font stacks; do not load web fonts from the network.
- **Scene.** An illustrated background in the ground (spotlights, stars, falling code, an equaliser, a sunburst, confetti, doodles, lasers, hills, a synthwave grid, palms, a notebook, speed lines, shards, cubes, a road, receipts, a pub, a pitch, a globe). Built from the 24 `.deep-scene i` pieces, which carry `--x`, `--y`, `--s`, `--d` and `--r`. A scene may move slowly; keep anything behind a title faint, and keep bright shapes off the left third where titles sit.
- **Texture.** A faint full-screen layer over the page, like a shader: `grain`, `scanlines`, `crt`, `halftone`, `vignette` or `holo`. It ignores the pointer. Keep it light: the edges of the page carry text, so a vignette darkens corners only.
- **Control and panel.** The shape, edge and lighting of buttons (`neon`, `bevel`, `hard-shadow`, `slant`, `bracket`, `scoreboard`, `stamp`, `pill-glass`) and cards (`glass`, `double`, `taped`, `terminal`, `tilted`, `receipt`, `notebook`, `jagged`, `scoreboard`, `polaroid`).
- **Heading.** How question and page titles are dressed: `shadow-stack`, `glow`, `gradient`, `highlighter`, `prompt`, `ransom`, `stamp`, `marquee` or `underline`. The text must stay as readable as plain.
- **Motion.** The `--ease-party` curve and how a panel arrives, once: `snappy`, `springy`, `floaty`, `glitchy`, `cinematic` or `mechanical`.
- **Align.** Headings `left` or `center`.

Choose the combination for the idea, not the last family. A new value goes in both `deep-skins.ts` and `theme-deep.css`, built only from the theme's colour variables. Reduced motion stops every scene and texture animation, turns panel arrivals into a short fade, and turns off glass blur.

## Icons

Icon packs are installed in `@26/web`. Search the live set before adding an icon, and import one icon at a time. Do not trace a logo from a brand site or a fan page. If Simple Icons has no slug, say so and use a generic icon.

Render with the offline Iconify component so a missing icon does not call the network:

```tsx
import { Icon } from "@iconify/react/dist/offline";
import car from "@iconify-icons/lucide/car";

<Icon icon={car} />;
```

From the repo root, the pinned installs are:

```
npm install @iconify/react@6.0.2 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/lucide@2.0.13 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/simple-icons@2.0.4 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/game-icons@2.0.0 -w @26/web
npm install @iconify-icons/mdi@2.0.0 -w @26/web
```

The import path is `@iconify-icons/{prefix}/{icon-name}`.

| Category                                                                                                                                            | Pack                                                           | Look for                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 26 basic, Personal to 26, Quiz and chaos, Dark and atmospheric, Light and nostalgic, Personal to the night, Everyday, School, Work, Musicians, Cars | [Lucide](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/lucide/)             | circle, user, circle-help, moon, sun, star, coffee, graduation-cap, briefcase, music, car |
| Cars, Work, Musicians, Games, and any named company, bank, platform, or artist                                                                      | [Simple Icons](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/simple-icons/) | nissan, toyota, and the brand slug                                                        |
| Games, and a pictogram that is not a publisher logo                                                                                                 | [Game Icons](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/game-icons/)     | dice, swords, cards                                                                       |
| A shape Lucide does not have                                                                                                                        | [Material Design Icons](https://icon-sets.iconify.design/mdi/) | the closest generic glyph                                                                 |

Persona, Anime, and Crossovers use Lucide for the tab. Use Simple Icons only when that studio, series, or platform has a slug. Game Icons does not include franchise characters.

The favicon stays the 26 basic mark.
